description: How the parties around a PastBook order relate to each other: how growth marketing and the app stores bring a family, traveller, Facebook archivist or gift giver to a one-click book, how consumers pay per product and ask support for help, how the operations manager routes print-ready jobs to partner printers and pays them, how partners report status and shipments back, and how Meta, Apple, Google, payment providers and carriers set the permissions, policies and events that the whole flow depends on.

relationTypes.name: Commercial
relationTypes.description: Campaigns, offers, app distribution and channel agreements that bring an order in

relationTypes.name: Operational
relationTypes.description: Photo permissions, order routing, production, delivery, reprints and refunds

relationTypes.name: Financial
relationTypes.description: Per-order payments, promo codes and gift cards, print partner fees and media spend

relationTypes.name: Information
relationTypes.description: Support questions, status and tracking events, reviews, root causes and platform policies

relations.name: Asks for help with the yearbook order
relations.description: Contacts support on WhatsApp, e-mail or chat about a missing photo, a page-count or cover question, an address fix or where the yearbook is, expecting an answer from the 24/7 team in one contact.

relations.name: Submits print-quality complaints for reprint
relations.description: Reports a large hardcover whose colours, binding or paper do not match the moment, with photos of the defect, and expects a reprint or refund decision quickly rather than a debate about the original file.

relations.name: Asks for Facebook import and privacy help
relations.description: Asks why a year is missing or captions did not import, how to reconnect Facebook Login after a permission change, and how to have the imported photos deleted after the book is printed.

relations.name: Chases delivery before the occasion
relations.description: Asks for tracking, a last-minute address change or an upgrade to faster shipping when the Christmas, Mother's Day or birthday date is close, often in the Q4 peak when contact volumes are highest.

relations.name: Arranges the reprint or refund
relations.description: Assesses the complaint against the print file and the partner's quality report, orders a reprint at the same or another facility or refunds the order, and confirms the new delivery window to the customer.

relations.name: Fixes the order and expedites the gift
relations.description: Changes the address or recipient while the order is still in production, asks operations to prioritise or re-route the job, shares the carrier tracking link and replies to the Trustpilot review when a gift still arrives late.

relations.name: Targets yearbook and Year in Review campaigns
relations.description: Sends push and e-mail reminders when a school year or calendar year closes, runs the Year in Review campaign with promo codes and free hardcover upgrades, and tests App Store creatives so the family orders one book per year.

relations.name: Runs holiday-deadline promotions and gift-card offers
relations.description: Publishes order-by dates per country, discounts on calendars, posters and large hardcovers, free-shipping upgrades and gift cards in ten languages and seven currencies, timed to the Q4 peak and Mother's Day.

relations.name: Promotes Facebook Photo Books years and reorders
relations.description: Runs paid social and e-mail campaigns that invite the archivist to print another year from 2009 to 2025 or to gift a copy of a past year, and explains the Facebook route now that Instagram import is gone.

relations.name: Delivers the gift within the published window
relations.description: Routes the job to a partner in the recipient's country, watches production against the order-by date and hands the parcel to a carrier so that the book, calendar or poster arrives inside the published 3 to 10 business-day window.

relations.name: Routes print-ready jobs and sets SLAs and capacity
relations.description: Sends imposed, preflighted print files with order data and packing slips through the partner API or hot folder, agrees production SLAs, defect thresholds, FSC paper and reserved capacity for the holiday peak per facility.

relations.name: Reports production status, shipments and defects
relations.description: Returns status callbacks per job, carrier tracking numbers, rejected files, quality incidents and daily capacity so the control tower can re-route jobs and update customers on delivery.

relations.name: Pays production and shipping fees per job
relations.description: Settles the partner's invoices for produced books, calendars and posters and the carrier cost per shipment, tracks unit production cost per book and format against target and charges back reprints caused by partner defects.

relations.name: Escalates reprint root causes and delivery failures
relations.description: Passes reprint cases, recurring defect patterns per facility and late or lost shipments per country to operations so routing rules, partner audits and carrier choices are corrected before the next peak.

relations.name: Sets app-store featuring, review and policy terms
relations.description: Apple and Google communicate review outcomes, featuring opportunities, privacy-label and billing rules, and Meta publishes platform terms and permission scopes that decide which campaigns and features can run.

relations.name: Grants Facebook Login and photo permissions
relations.description: Meta authenticates the archivist and grants PastBook access to albums, timeline pictures, cover and profile photos and mobile uploads within the scope Meta allows, and withdraws access when permissions or platform policies change.

relations.name: Buys paid media and app-store placements
relations.description: Spends the acquisition budget on Meta and Google ads, Apple Search Ads and app-store placements, and pays platform fees on in-app purchases, measured as blended CAC and return on ad spend.

relations.name: Distributes the app through the App Store and Google Play
relations.description: Apple and Google list, review and feature the PastBook 1-Click Photo Book app, handle the install and in-app billing, and show the ratings that decide whether a parent taps install.

relations.name: Pays per book at checkout, releasing production
relations.description: Pays for the small or large hardcover, extra pages and shipping by Visa, Mastercard, American Express or PayPal in one of seven currencies; production starts on payment and funds the partner print and shipping cost.

relations.name: Redeems promo codes and buys gift cards
relations.description: Applies seasonal discount codes and free-shipping upgrades at checkout and buys gift cards for family who have the photos, which turns marketing's promotions into paid orders and prepaid balances.

relations.name: Rates the app and reviews on Trustpilot
relations.description: Responds to in-app rating prompts and Trustpilot invitations after delivery, which feeds the App Store and Google Play ratings and the 4.5 TrustScore that marketing uses in campaigns and monitors as a KPI.

relations.name: Sends carrier tracking and payment events
relations.description: Carriers push scan and delivery events per parcel and payment providers push authorisation, capture and chargeback events, which drive order status, delivery performance per country and the tracking shown to customers.
